title: South Korea's PIPC finds no violations or leaks in pre-merger data checks of Korean Air, Gmarket and Remember & Company
date_note: Newsis's article of 26 November reports the commission disclosing the results that day; it was deliberated on 25 November.
geo_basis: country as stated by the source; pin at the capital
summary: South Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission said it completed preliminary inspections of Korean Air, Gmarket and Remember & Company, which are going through mergers or ownership changes, and found no legal violations or unauthorised leaks so far, Newsis reports. It recommended that personal data held by Asiana Airlines be destroyed without delay once its processing purpose is achieved, and issued guidance on transferring personal data in mergers.
plain: South Korea's data protection regulator says it checked three companies undergoing mergers or ownership changes and has found no violations or leaks so far.
exec: The regulator found no violations or leaks so far at three companies and issued guidance on moving personal data in mergers.

validation.note: One publisher (Newsis) relaying the commission's announcement; the commission's own release was not read.
